newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico stocks up on follow-through, confidence.
newsitem.headline: Mexico stocks up on follow-through, confidence.

text.p: Mexican stocks opened up in slow, but firm early trade on momentum carried over from the prior session, as domestic and foreign investors bought on continuing economic and political confidence, traders said.

"There's a strong feel-good factor in the market. Dealers no longer see the (mid-term) elections as being a problem, the forex and money markets are relatively stable. The market looks firm," a desk trader said.
The leading IPC share index .MXX was up 16.54 points in the opening minutes of trade, or 0.38 percent, at 4,370.21. Trading volume .TV.MX was quiet at 723,000 shares.
Mexico will hold mid-term elections on July 6 for the lower house of Congress, one quarter of the Senate, several state governors and Mexico City mayor for the first time in modern history.
"Foreigners are buying again," a floor trader said. "ADRs are up in New York, the Dow Jones is up, it looks good."
Dealers said market heavyweight Telmex and cement stock Cemex led the blue chip advance.
Telmex was up 16 centavos to 18.96 pesos, while the telecom's ADRs had gained 1/4 to 47-1/2. The Dow Jones was meanwhile up 16.74 points to 7,793.80.
Carso Grupo Telecom, Telmex's holding company, was a prominent early leader, up 25 centavos to 30.50 pesos.
Cemex B shares were up 80 centavos at 37.10 pesos. Dealers said cement stocks benefitted from strong industrial output figures released on Tuesday that showed heavy building activity.
On the broad market, 39 stocks traded in total, of which gainers outnumbered sliders by 26 to five.
Dealers also drew attention to cable maker Grupo Industrial Camesa, up 2 centavos to 4.92 pesos in relatively brisk early trade.

"Camesa had lagged the market, and foreigners are stepping in to buy stragglers. It's also a liquid market -- just look at the demand for companies that have gone public, like Biper," a desk trader said.
Paging company Biper went public on Thursday. Its B shares were ahead 16 centavos at 3.34 pesos in early trade.
